September 2026 Portfolio Review

September continued with a solid march upwards of another 10%+ for my holdings. I didn't make any buys or sells during the month, only my regular weekly contributions. $SNOW had earnings at the beginning of the month, $MU had their earnings at the end of the month. 

Earlier in the month I did an exercise trying to steelman the bear cases for AI that most concern to me. https://t.co/qhDqpWrCzc 

Nominal is pure % change, Real takes into account contributions made. 

Monthly Gain: Up 13.0% Nominal // Up 12.2% Real 
Yearly Gain: Up 75.2% Nominal // Up 50.3% Real 
All Time Gain (from 2019): Up 78.5%

$NBIS // Up 20.3% // 45.8% Allocation 

Nebius continues to headline the portfolio by a large margin. Fastest growth one can find, in an industry/sector expanding exponentially, with a leadership team who is executing flawlessly. They are a vertically integrated AI cloud company that designs, builds, and operates its own data centers, GPU clusters, and full software stack, renting AI compute to everyone from startups to the biggest companies in the world, Microsoft and Meta.

There was a decent amount of news this month. Starting on 9/8, with Palantir naming Nebius their preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, so Palantir's commercial customers can run their own models with control over compute, data, and the models themselves, enabled by Nebius. While there is no dollar value, contract, or concrete timeline, this announcement is further validation that Nebius is trusted by major institutions. 

Then, in mid-September, came the huge announcement from major AI executives calling for slower pace in AI development. Dario Amodei initiated the call with a detailed essay, "We Must Pace the Frontier." OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and other leaders followed in agreement. Many are skeptical that these major AI names are attempting "regulatory capture," trying to close the door behind them to lock in their positions as top dog in the sector, as they face more pressure from potentially open source models. Other people are more inclined to take them at their word and share in the fear that we could irreversibly mess up this moment if we don't take care during AI's initial development. I fall more in the latter's camp, but see both arguments. However, when it comes to Nebius and my other AI stocks, I do not see being cautious and intentional about AI development in any shade of negative light. In fact, I think this intentionality would be much better overall compared to a no-holds-barred race to develop "the best" model at all costs, or reach AGI/RSI/SGI first etc. Bottom line is: this technology is inevitable, so we should move forward with purpose. 

That inevitability gained another proof point on 9/23 as Nebius announced another round of Token Factory price increases equaling up 18.3% on average. Nebius also launched a pilot to try a new idea that involves auctioning their endpoints off to let the market set the price for capacity. During the pilot they cleared their highest Blackwell price to date. Demand is sky high. Live compute remains the bottleneck and customers are willing to pay. Also on 9/23, Nebius joined CoreWeave in the Platinum tier of SemiAnalysis' ClusterMAX ratings, a high technical benchmark confirmation. Finally on 9/30, 
AIB Data Centers signed a capacity contract with Nebius. This partnership, and others like it, will help build out the needed capacity that Nebius will operate. These contracts help spread the CapEx load so that risk isn't solely on Nebius and the funding isn't through pure debt or dilution. 

Nebius has done nothing but affirm my belief in the company. I expect to add more on weakness, despite how much of my portfolio it already makes up. 

$MU // Up 15.1% // 18.7% Allocation 

Micron is the second largest position in my portfolio for good reason. They are one of three global DRAM makers and the only US based HBM producer, supplying the memory and storage that have become the tightest bottleneck in the entire AI buildout. Their business is rapidly shifting from cyclical commodity to multi-year contracts. I am making a strong bet on them because I don't think the market has fully digested this company's role in the AI buildout and what it means economically. Their valuation is comically low right now, whichever way you look at it; TTM P/S = 9.1, Forward P/S = 4.7, TTM P/E = 14.5, Forward P/E = 6.1. Think about it this way, Micron trades at 6x forward earnings, while projected to out-earn every single Mag-7 company in quarterly operating income, who trade at 25-35x their forward earnings. The gap is the market pricing in a bunch of supply coming in to satiate the demand spike we're in the midst of right now. I simply don't think that supply will have as negative an impact, as quickly as is being projected right now. 

Micron had Q4 earnings on 9/30, the last day of the month. They had another blowout quarter. Revenue came in at $54.2B, beating last quarter's guide of $50.0B by 8.5%. Revenue was up 31% QoQ and 379% YoY. Gross Margin (which is the metric to watch for commoditization) was 87% versus the 86% guide. Memory prices continue to increase along with demand. DDR5 prices are up 100%+ in 2026 alone. Forecasts saw another 10-15% increase for DRAM ($39.8B {73% of revenue, +343% YoY}) and 15-20% increase for NAND ($14.1B {+526% YoY}) prices from this quarter to the next one. These prices are not commoditizing yet, they are rising and accelerating. Their Strategic Customer Agreements signed this quarter was 26, up from 16 last quarter. 75% of expected 2027 output is already committed. 2028 output is already being negotiated now. Not only did they knock this quarter out of the park, they also gave impressive guidance. Next quarter revenue guidance is $61.5B, (13% QoQ, 350% YoY), gross margins of 86.3% (which they called the floor for FY27), and said supply-demand will be tighter in 2027 and 2028, than 2026, with no current visibility into when it might balance out again. That is bullish beyond belief in my view. Again, especially at this valuation, these business numbers are a screaming buy. 

$NVDA // Up 5.6% // 12.8% Allocation  

Nvidia is the leading designer of GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software stacks that constitute most of the world's AI compute. They are the central supplier, investor, and platform layer of the entire AI buildout. The stock has been mostly stagnant for a while, but I am happy holding as the business continues its unprecedented run as the massive leviathan powering the entire emergence of an AI-enabled world. 

On 9/2, they agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B (including a $1B retention program), a distribution hub of open-source AI, where models, datasets, and apps actually live. This helps anchor the open model ecosystem to Nvidia hardware and CUDA by default, widening their moat a little. On 9/9, they expanded their AI infrastructure into a new geography through a partnership that gets Australia's data center ecosystem involved. A day later on 9/10, they released details on a Palantir partnership about sovereign intelligence for critical supply chains. That same day it was reported that Nvidia was reportedly weighing a $10B backing of Anthropic's IPO. This aligns with the circular financing bear case that I discussed earlier this month. Making equity stakes in the labs that buy their own chips is a move that comes with both advantages and risks. Side note, if Anthropic does IPO, I will most definitely look into starting a ~5% position or so. 

On 9/17, Nvidia announced a $2B investment into Brookfield's AI fund to help meet upcoming energy and physical demands for the AI buildout. Then later in the month, it was reported that China might allow Alibaba to buy Nvidia RTX chips and on 9/28, a Chinese state-backed firm disclosed a Blackwell chip deal. These are both signs that the export-control wall is cracking from all sides. China is permitting these purchases, while companies are disclosing those purchases openly. Current Nvidia projections exclude China, so any progress in the country is additive to the TAM. Responding to recent safety incidents, on 9/28 they launched the 'Open Agent Safety Platform', to monitor agent behavior, providing a governance layer and smartly trying to monetize AI safety. Also on 9/28, the largest buyback authorization increase in history was announced at $150B, bringing the total remaining to $235B. The fact that they have this much cash to buy stock through FY28 and are still compounding revenue at 100% YoY, while pointing to 70% growth in 2028, is absolutely insane and previews that they believe the stock is mispriced too low right now. I agree.

$RDDT // Down 1.3% // 10.0% Allocation  

Reddit is a platform of niche communities whose moat in the AI era is authentic human-generated content and the communities themselves, built and centered around any topic imaginable. 95% advertising revenue, 5% data licensing. They have had impressive revenue metrics with 6 quarters in a row of 60%+ YoY growth, paired with gross margins over 91%, plus a low valuation of 10.2 TTM P/S and 7.3 Forward P/S, which had been cut in half from 20-22x in late 2025. Stock has not responded well recently, but I believe the ticker will catch up to the numbers soon enough and reverse this multiple compression we've seen. 

Not too much news this month. On 9/10, Piper Sandler data showed August user growth hit its fastest monthly pace of 2026, a datapoint that indicates improvement in one of the most worrisome metrics of the last few reports (user growth, specifically DAUs and WAUs). Then on 9/22, Reddit got a win in court against Anthropic over data-scraping litigation. It's only a procedural ruling rather than a merits based one, but Reddit's chief legal officer Ben Lee, said "the ruling sends a message that AI companies can't scrape people's information without clear limits on how the data gets used." Apart from the stellar revenue numbers, my main investment thesis on Reddit, is that their data is severely underpriced to the point that they can charge at least 5-10x more for it, probably even more than that. Every win in court like this strengthens Reddit's negotiating position for repricing their data access. 

$NET // Up 22.6% // 7.3% Allocation

Cloudflare is positioning themselves as the infrastructure, controls, and payment rail for the agentic internet. They operate a global edge network with CDN, DNS, DDoS, zero trust, and Workers. They are a traditional SaaS plus consumption business. One of my longest held companies. Solid, reliable performer with a sky high valuation (49.5 TTM P/S, 38.1 Forward P/S), which led to some trimming last month. 

On 9/2, Cursor, a leading AI company, launched Cursor Cloud Agents on the Cloudflare Sandboxes execution layer. Confirmation that they are taking a part of the agentic workload pie. The day after on 9/3, they partnered with OpenAI on their Daybreak models for AI-powered vulnerability management at the edge. This is their security revenue getting an AI-native upgrade rather than being disrupted by it. Good sign that they are adapting well to the new AI economy. 

Biggest announcement of the month came on 9/9, when Cloudflare management announced a raise in their "North Star" growth target from 40% to 50%. That is the exact type of ambitious announcement you want to see. 36% was the YoY number they hit last time, so significant acceleration may be ahead! The same day they disclosed 2M developer adds QoQ (record pace), 80% of major AI enterprise infrastructure companies as customers, and an ongoing shift from subscription to consumption revenue. 'Monetization Gateway' and 'Cloudflare Wallets' introduced as two new products to take advantage of the agent economy and autonomous agent transactions made amongst each other. 

There were a few other product announcements. On 9/15, Cloudflare launched new crawler controls that split AI traffic into Search, Agent, and Training categories, with a 'Disallow AI Training' setting, an 'Accountable' crawler designation, and defaults that block training and agent crawlers on ad-supported pages, so multi-purpose bots like Googlebot can be blocked from training even while search indexing stays allowed. This makes Cloudflare the toll booth between publishers and AI companies by breaking the bundling that let training scrapes hide behind search. On 9/25, they disclosed a small cross-tenant data-isolation vulnerability that they quickly fixed in 'Containers' and 'Sandboxes'. Looking at other future long term growth potential, on 9/29 they launched a public 'Certificate Authority' for the post-quantum web, as well as a Deutsche Telekom partnership for a "secure and resilient internet" and European distribution. 

$ALAB // Up 28.1% // 6.3% Allocation  

Astera Labs is a fabless designer of connectivity silicon for AI racks. Product line includes: Aries PCIe retimers, Taurus Ethernet signal conditioners, Leo CXL memory controllers, and Scorpio fabric switches routing traffic between GPUs, with content-per-accelerator as the growth driver. They've always been pretty expensive valuation wise (50.6 TTM P/S, 23.2 Forward P/S), but as revenue continues to build, the forward metrics actually look more reasonable. Especially with the pre-announcement that Astera expects Scorpio to become its biggest product line a quarter ahead of schedule. On pure revenue acceleration trajectory, this may have the second steepest potential curve, only behind Nebius. 

On 9/15, they launched the Leo X-Series, expanding their Leo Smart Memory Controller family for agentic AI and general purpose cloud workloads, pairing with Scorpio X-Series fabric switches to enable memory expansion and pooling. This was explicitly pitched as optimizing 'token economics' as memory footprints explode amid tight supply. Better and more efficient memory is drastically needed to address the current demand bottleneck. When DRAM is the most expensive, scarcest input in the rack, silicon that pools and reuses memory across accelerators stops being a nice-to-have and becomes a cost-of-goods lever for every hyperscaler. Interestingly, this is the other side of the coin when compared to Micron. The memory crisis that powers Micron's pricing is simultaneously creating Leo's market. Astera is helping with this product announcement. Astera is bound to make a ton of money on it too, but it will also allow Micron to sell more volume once they actually have the supply. A massive win-win in my view. 

$CRWD // Up 22.8% // 5.5% Allocation  

Crowdstrike runs Falcon, a cloud-native cybersecurity platform delivering endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and SIEM protection through a single agent. They are my steady cybersecurity anchor, now pivoting hard to securing AI agents themselves. Very high valuation at 51.4 TTM P/S and 41.7 Forward P/S. 

The beginning of the month was headlined by Fal.Con 2026, their yearly conference which included a dozen plus announcements, 10,000+ attendees, and 4,000+ organizations. Some important announcements include: Falcon Guardian, their headline product for discovering and securing AI agents across an enterprise. It's an entirely new module that is attempting to create the first solution to 'agentic security' right as the need for it is arising. Impressive agility for a large company and why they are a leader in their field. ; Agentic IdP, which gives AI agents trusted identities through the Falcon Identity control plane. ; SafeMind, announced with Jensen Huang on stage, a purpose-built agentic AI system for cybersecurity that combines offensive and defensive models in a continuous learning loop. ; Google Cloud AI-security expansion with a 'Cyber Superintelligence Lab'. ; an https://t.co/v1egDDtCjA partnership to make Falcon their enterprise AI security foundational blueprint. ; and an expanded OpenAI partnership to ensure Codex agents and GPT-5.6's cyber model comes to Falcon. 

At Citi's Global TMT Conference on 9/10, Crowdstrike CFO Podbere argued AI is reshaping security spending in their favor with stronger demand, faster module adoption, while acknowledging margin pressure and Microsoft competition. On 9/17 and 9/24, they were named a leader in Forrester 'External Threat Intelligence' and 'Proactive Security Platforms', ranked highest in Strategy. On 9/28, their Nvidia partnership expanded to cover the entire AI stack, securing a seat inside Nvidia's agent-security architecture. Then on 9/29, Falcon was officially listed on the OpenAI Marketplace. Falcon is also already on Claude Marketplace. 

$SNOW // Up 7.1% // 3.6% Allocation  

Snowflake is an AI Data Cloud with consumption-priced storage, compute, and data sharing across AWS/Azure/GCP, now layered with Cortex, the CoWork knowledge-worker agent, and the CoCo coding agent, positioning itself as the governed control plane for enterprise AI. They are a durable, steady compounder that is reaccelerating at scale and currently has a historically decent valuation (22.1 TTM P/S, 16.8 Forward P/S). 

Big news came early for Snowflake as they had their Q2 earnings on 9/2 at the beginning of the month. Product revenue was $1.49B (up 37% YoY), beating last quarter's guidance of $1.42B by 5.2%. While those aren't the fastest numbers we've seen, it was the third consecutive quarter of product revenue growth acceleration. CoWork and CoCo, were given special shoutouts as they led a meaningful step up in AI revenue with new workloads and consumption. Their product revenue guide for FY27 was raised from $5.84B (31% growth) --> $6.07B (36% growth) and would be a 3.9% full-year raise. Very big considering their current scale and usually minuscule raises. NRR slightly increased from 125% --> 126%, 828 customers spending over $1M (up 27% YoY), and 829 of the Forbes Global 2000 as customers. RPO grew 30% YoY to $9.0B, but declined sequentially from $9.21B (38% YoY).  

Macro: 

In last month's macro section I spent a lot of time discussing some theories and possibilities surrounding the future of AI and its impact on the economy and the world more generally. TLDR; there are just as many reasons to be fearful and cautious as there are to be excited. This month I wanted to shift the conversation back to the K shaped economy exacerbating wealth inequality through asset ownership, stagflation, and the massive potential energy behind the stocks in my portfolio. 

Starting with the K shaped economy. I am increasingly of the opinion that wealth inequality, standards of living, and the general gap between the haves and have nots will continue to get much worse before it gets better (at current trajectory). I see a world where consumer wage growth tops out at 3-4% per year, while assets compound at 50-100%. AI is structurally shifting income from labor to capital, which is already the direction money normally flows. The productivity gains go to whomever owns the compute, memory, and models. 

One overall macro question I had during my bear case analysis was about who sustains demand for these AI products? My fear is about a weak consumer base that can't support the infrastructure we're currently building. Right now, corporations are buying from corporations. The $730B hyperscaler capex buildout, the prepayments for Nebius and Micron, commitments from Nvidia, etc. It's a closed capital loop that, right now, doesn't need healthy consumers yet. There are a few ways this closed loop might open up: 
1) AI productivity appears in the real economy. GDP, margins, and business metrics go up and show true gains that validate the CapEx spending, and in turn, leads to more spend. 
2) Consumer side cracks. If real wages continue to trend negative, eventually the worker economy will bleed into the AI economy and spend will decrease. Advertising is one way, enterprise software is another. 
3) Political/government intervention. A world where companies continue to hit record metrics, while paychecks shrink in real terms is not politically nor mathematically stable. Release valves can be done through either redistribution (capital gains, windfall taxes, AI taxes, antitrust) or it can be done through populist rupture and upheaval of current systems/institutions. 

I see each of these happening to some extent. Hopefully we can address some of the root causes sooner rather than later... 

The next topic is stagflation. The current economic landscape shows some striking similarities to what the US dealt with during the 1970s. Stagnant growth (other than AI) + persistent inflation + rising unemployment + supply shocks. We've had inflation above target rates for 5 years in a row now. The recent bout of inflation being exacerbated by tariffs and war-driven energy costs, which followed immediately after a successful soft-landing that balanced rate hikes and unemployment from 2022-2024. Self-induced pain on inflation. Payrolls decelerated, unemployment ticked up very slightly to 4.2% (10/2 event), wage growth is at a five year low and negative in real terms. The Fed is facing the same trap from the 1970s: hike rates and you risk damaging an already weakening labor market; hold or lower rates and you make inflation worse. I worry that stagflation occurs for labor, while the asset economy inflates, again all going back to the K shaped economy described above.

Inflation was unchanged from July. August CPI up 0.1% MoM, 3.4% YoY for headline inflation. Hotter than expected leading to the Fed's decision to hike rates by 25bps to 3.75%-4.00%. This follows an August jobs report of +133k, above forecasts and reversing from a negative month in July (but recent 10/2 report has worse numbers). It was accompanied by a statement saying the rate increase supports a "timelier return to 2%." The impact on my stocks could be negligible or it could massively cut valuations like in 2022. I do not anticipate rate increases or decreases to impact how I invest. 

To conclude the macro section I wanted to briefly discuss a 'vibe' I'm sensing right now. This is purely intuition and gut feeling, but it seems like my stocks (AI mostly) are coiling. This may sound greedy considering the gains that I've seen this year already, but I can't help but feel 1) that the overall macro economy is holding my portfolio back and that valuations are slightly compressed because of it and 2) growth will be a lot more explosive and last longer than even the rosiest estimates are taking into account. 

Not only are current valuations pretty low, but I also think 2028 and beyond are mispriced due to the market's current bet that supply will flood and normalize demand by then. I just don't see that in the numbers right now. I see a massive economic disruption that has only just begun. I sense that Mr. Market is just waiting for the right macroeconomic conditions to massively rip upward.

Surge AI 的新基准论文：DAYJOB: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Professional Work。

他们用 130 个真实工作任务组成了新的基准，包含医疗 50、金融 80。

全部由有实战经验的专家搭建，高级投资组合经理、基建融资专家、儿科内分泌科医生。

他们的新基准及尽模拟真实显示的工作场景和流程：

① 第一点就是他们的基准中对于工作发出的请求很短，而且文件极多。
比如同事的请求：“新客户首份基金报告今天要发，看下有没有问题，写个简短 memo”。
并且所需要的各种信息是需要全在工作区里自己挖的，不会给予信息源等等的。每个任务会盛放 8–122 个文件，这里面包含了很多无关的文件和材料。
比如：急诊任务里 9 个 PDF 有 7 个是行政表格，此外还有 2019 年的评估用在 2026 年的提案、memo 写 3.25% 但 CFO 后来的聊天截图说 5.25%，这类的混乱的和冲突的信息都包含在内。

② 第二点就是验收比较严格，结果中必须要专家的 rubric 全过才算过。
每个任务取其中位 47–58 条二值判据，judge 在容器里打开交付文件、重算数值、逐条给证据，如果说有任何一条不满足就算做本轮是失败的。
他们还加入了一个 "禁止项"：如果错误的把按政策正确定价的拆股股票报成发布阻碍，那么会直接判负。

③ 第三点，他们的这个新基准的每个任务都有专业人士进行工作预估出拉一个大概的时间需求作为对照：
医疗每个任务大约 1 3 .6 小时；金融是 1 6 .6 小时。

一共对于13 家开发者 30 个配置进行了测试。最后的结果是：
最强的是 Claude Opus 5.5，通过率 24.7%（医疗），23.9%（金融）；
它的而且中位配置只有 0.6%/2.5%；
19 个配置两个领域都低于 5%

这个成绩可以说非常差劲了。最强的模型才 25%，中位不到 3%。
明显的说明 现在的模型对于专业的全流程无过多干预的任务距离自动化还远，跟目前的各种乐观叙事是有大反差的。

「人工智能因為有『人工』這兩個字，聽起來就是假的。」(When you say artificial intelligence, it’s ‘artificial’)
​
Donald Trump這樣說到，於是他大筆一揮簽了行政命令：聯邦政府以後改口，把 AI 改稱 SI（Super Intelligence，超級智慧）。
​
9 月 29 日，Trump 把黃仁勳、Elon Musk、Mark Zuckerberg、Dario Amodei 等科技巨頭全找進了白宮。
​
同一天晚上，Musk 和黃仁勳同台對談。但如果你剝開公關說辭，這場峰會其實充滿了政治算計、華爾街的數學題，以及關起門來的激烈交鋒。
​
▋ 從「資料中心」到「智慧工廠」
​
晚上的對談，黃仁勳一句話為整場定調：「我們以前叫它們資料中心，因為那時候主要存資料。但我們現在蓋的，其實是超級智慧工廠（SI Factories）。」
​
為什麼改名這麼重要？
​
過去幾年，資料中心（Data Center）在美國地方上就是惹人怨的代名詞：耗電、耗水、噪音大。
​
但工廠（Factories）聽起來完全不同，工廠意味著藍領就業、地方稅收、小鎮復興。黃仁勳把一個科技基建，包裝成了美國重新工業化的契機。
​
Musk 馬上接力：xAI 在曼菲斯的超級運算中心讓當地稅收翻倍、工作機會多到缺工。
​
這套敘事的聽眾很明確：小鎮居民、地方議會、工會。因為 AI 擴張真正的瓶頸，排在晶片和電力後面的，是「社會許可」，也就是居民願不願意讓你蓋在他家旁邊。
​
▋ 那張沒有實質用處的協定
​
當天早上，Trump 和六大巨頭簽了一份《超級智慧白宮協定》。
​
文件只有一頁、大約三百字，寫了四層承諾：監控模型能力、內部確認控管有效、引入外部稽核、董事會設獨立委員會。
​
說白了，這份協定在實務上沒有太大用處。沒有罰則，沒有監管機關會上門開罰。
​
Trump 自己說它「道德上有約束力」，文件最後留了一句「以後或許寫進法律」。
​
對科技公司來說，簽這張紙幾乎零成本，卻換到監管喘息空間。對白宮來說，不用過法案就能展現「我們有在管」。各取所需，完美交易。
​
▋ 草坪上的團結，與閉門室裡的交鋒
​
這場峰會最有張力的一幕，發生在鏡頭之外。
​
過去幾週，衝突很明確：Anthropic 執行長 Dario Amodei 不斷喊「放慢腳步」，Trump 陣營則暗示這是藉口，美國不能停。
​
這次大會，兩人關起門來談了一場。根據《華爾街日報》，黃仁勳等高層也在場，直接質問 Dario：為什麼你總把風險講得那麼末日？Dario 沒有退讓：對公眾必須誠實。
​
但簽完字走到草坪上，畫面又變成大團結。
​
記者把麥克風遞給 Dario，他沒收回「放慢」的警告，但語氣收成了：「我們可以贏，而且安全地贏。」
​
Trump 在旁邊立刻幫腔：「Dario 棒極了，吃過飯後他同意大家的看法。」
​
這對投資人意味著什麼？短期內，聯邦層面出現硬管制（限制算力、凍結訓練）的機率大幅下降。華府和同業聯手告訴安全派：先跑了再說。
​
▋ 1 GW 電力 = 600 億美元產出？
​
監管鬆綁了，戰場就是實體基建。
​
晚上最精彩的部分，是 Musk 和黃仁勳現場算了一筆「電力經濟學」。
​
Musk 的算法：美國平均用電約 500 GW，每新增 5 GW（多 1% 用電），大約帶動 1% GDP。
​
黃仁勳接球：1% GDP 是 3,000 億美元，5 GW 對 3,000 億，等於每 1 GW 一年創造約 600 億美元經濟產出。他還補了一句：「算術是我們擅長的。」
​
Musk 順道拉中國當對照：中國發電量約美國三倍（實際約 2.3 倍）。結論是：美國軟體領先，但長期要贏，必須在本土同時掌握電力和晶片產能。
​
▋ 這是一場大型「敘事矯正」
​
叫 AI 還是 SI，不重要。那份協定，也沒什麼實質意義。
​
這場峰會，更像是白宮聯手科技巨頭的一場「敘事矯正」。
​
過去幾週，Amodei 不斷喊放慢、談末日，讓華府不安。所以白宮把所有人找來，關起門質問，草坪上拍大團結照，目的只有一個：把公眾注意力從「AI 有多危險」，硬生生拉回「美國必須贏」。
​
他們要修正 Amodei 種下的恐懼，重新定義這項技術的身分：這是一場能帶來就業、稅收和國運繁榮的比賽，美國非贏不可。
​
這個主題收錄在我週末筆記中，裡面還有更把這週幾個值得深聊的題目一次攤開來談，完全免費閱讀：
​
主題一 | Meta 的千億美元大棋：從「注意力網路」到「AI 代理人經濟」
​
1.1| 挖角MongoDB CEO，Meta準備進軍企業市場？
​
1.2| Meta 正在盯著小企業的「數位大腦」
​
主題二 | 為甚麼 AMD 要花 82 億美元買一家沒有營收的公司？
​
主題三 | Trump把科技大佬找來，就為了把AI改成SI？
​
主題四 | 東芝大舉擴產，存儲供不應求準備翻轉了？這篇的延伸版，我把 NAND、DRAM、HBM 的結構差異也一起拆了。
​
週末筆記完全免費，你只要訂閱，就能每個星期收到我的看法，連結在下方。
​
- KP

Agent 沒有一個總冠軍。同一家模型，換一套工具、換一個評測版本，名次就會變。對創業者有用的，是按任務拆，不是按品牌站隊。

長時間改程式庫，目前仍是 Claude 最穩。Claude Opus 5.5 在多家對照裡排在代理程式前面：要自己找檔案、反覆用工具、維持計畫不跑偏。公開對照裡，它在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 約 66%，高於 GPT-6 Astra 的約 58%、Claude Fable 5.1 的約 56%。價格大約是每百萬 token 輸入 4 美元、輸出 20 美元，比最貴那層便宜，又夠能扛長任務。日常量大，可以降到 Sonnet 5.5。

跨軟體、要自己操作電腦，OpenAI 更合適。GPT-6 Astra 是旗艦，強項不是「多寫幾行程式」，而是程式、研究、點介面串在一起。它輸出 token 往往更少，但單價高，大約 10／50 美元。科學類終端任務它會贏。日常代理不必天天用它，卡住再升級。預算要控，用 GPT-6 Sol，大約 2／10 美元，當主力夠用。

便宜、要跑很多步的分流，看 Google 和開源。Gemini 3.8 Flash 上下文長、價格低，適合量大的子代理：抽資料、查文件、做初篩。DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM、Qwen 在部分終端榜上很接近前沿，適合當子代理和備援，不適合當唯一主腦。開源的優點是可自架、單價低；缺點是產品外殼、工具呼叫和失敗重試要自己補。

Grok 4.7 落在中價帶，工具呼叫夠用，適合要接搜尋、要快迭代的代理。共享的程式代理榜上，它通常落後 Opus 和 Astra，不要拿它當最難程式庫的第一選擇。

還有一類不該跟上面比。Jev 這類系統一模型不寫回覆，只做分類並給機率：這封信該不該轉人工、這步工具該不該執行。它省的是判斷成本，不是寫作能力。

一個能上線的代理，大致是這樣拆的：

路由和護欄用便宜模型，或專門的機率模型。
日常執行用 Sonnet、Sol 或 Flash。
難的程式庫任務交給 Opus。
要操作電腦、跨應用的長任務交給 Astra。
再留一個別家模型和一個開源模型當備援。
看成績時只比同一套評測。Terminal-Bench 2、3、4 不能橫向比。Agent 死在工具、權限和重試，不主要死在聊天分數。每月重跑自己的任務，比記榜單有用。

OUSD could become an important financial bridge for the Pi ecosystem, but we must distinguish between an actual integration agreement and what is technically possible.

The five possibilities identified represent a potential progression from wallet integration to international payments. 

However, the critical question is whether OUSD will operate alongside Pi as a settlement asset or whether it will influence Pi's internal valuation.

For the GCV community, this distinction is particularly important. 

A dollar-linked stablecoin could facilitate payments without necessarily becoming the benchmark for Pi's purchasing power.

1. What has actually been announced?

On September 30, 2026, Pi Network announced its partnership with Open Standard to explore Pioneer rewards and broader OUSD utility within the Pi ecosystem.

However, no detailed technical integration, rollout schedule or reward structure has been confirmed.
https://t.co/DjDvIchg8u

OUSD itself is already operational. 

According to Open Standard, it supports Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo, with payment and settlement infrastructure offered through major financial technology providers. 

Pi is not yet listed among its native blockchains.
https://t.co/wrr924tltW

2. My assessment of the five possible integrations
The partnership explicitly identifies rewards as an area to explore. 

Eligibility, reward amounts and payment assets remain unknown.

A). OUSD → Pioneer rewards Most directly supported

Developers could introduce OUSD payments, subscriptions or incentives, initially through external payment infrastructure.

B). OUSD → Pi Apps Plausible next step

Direct support would require compatible asset issuance, integration or bridging infrastructure, alongside appropriate security measures.

C). OUSD → Pi Wallet Technically possible

Merchants could accept Pi from customers while optionally settling invoices in OUSD, provided conversion liquidity and compliant payment services exist.

D). OUSD → Merchant settlement
Commercially attractive

OUSD already targets international payments. Connecting that infrastructure to Pi would require additional agreements, conversion facilities and regulatory compliance.

E). OUSD → Cross-border settlement Longer-term opportunity

These are assessments of possible developments, not confirmed implementation commitments.

3. How Pi and OUSD could work together

Illustrative architecture

Pi Economy (Commerce, applications and Pioneer transactions) 

→ Optional conversion and settlement layer (Liquidity providers, payment services and regulatory compliance) 

→ OUSD (Dollar-linked settlement and international payment infrastructure)

Consider an international merchant selling merchandise through a Pi application.

The merchant could display a price in Pi and receive Pi from a Pioneer. An independent settlement provider could then convert the payment into OUSD, allowing the merchant to receive a dollar-linked asset.

This arrangement would allow Pi to function as the customer's payment currency while OUSD serves as an optional settlement instrument.

However, conversion would still require an exchange rate between Pi and OUSD. 

That rate would introduce an external dollar-linked reference, even if the original transaction were denominated in Pi.

4. What does this mean for GCV?

This partnership neither confirms nor invalidates GCV.

A Pi-centric DEX can express token prices in Pi, but that arrangement alone cannot establish a fixed purchasing power for Pi or prevent external exchange prices from influencing commerce.

GCV could remain a voluntary community pricing convention. 

For it to function reliably alongside OUSD, participating merchants would need sustainable pricing, sufficient liquidity and clear arrangements for handling differences between community valuations and external exchange rates.

The most promising possibility is a system in which Pi supports everyday economic activity while OUSD provides optional international payment infrastructure.

My expectation: 

Pioneer rewards and application-level experiments are the most logical developments to watch first. 

Direct Pi Wallet support and cross-border settlement would represent much more substantial integration milestones.

The decisive announcement to watch for is not simply OUSD appearing in the Pi ecosystem but: 

It is an official explanation of how Pi-to-OUSD conversion, liquidity, merchant settlement and Pioneer rewards will actually operate.

我记得半年前我说自己不怎么 Review PR 了，评论区很多人不认同，觉得这样不靠谱。现在再看，不 Review PR 的人越来越多。比如我刚看的这期播客，在 SpaceXAI 做 Grok Bot 的 Lauren Tan，一个月合并 2500 个 PR，也是不逐个 Review 的：晚上让 AI 自己检查、自己合并，第二天早上她再抽查。

不 Review 不等于不管质量，她靠另外两个办法来保证：
一是让 AI 能像真人用户一样把程序用一遍，自己发现问题；
二是给代码定下很多规矩，让 AI 很难写出烂代码。

她把自己这套做法写成了一组 Skill，公开了出来，叫 pstack。

顺便说一下，这期播客的主持人 Matt Pocock 原本是知名的编程课讲师，他公开的技能库在代码托管网站 GitHub 上有二十多万个星标，是最受欢迎的技能库之一，所以这期算是两位同行对谈。Lauren 之前在 Meta 做网页开发框架 React，今年 3 月加入 AI 编程工具公司 Cursor；Cursor 今年 8 月被 SpaceX 收购，并入旗下的 AI 部门 SpaceXAI。

根据播客的内容，我把 Lauren 的这套做法简单总结一下，我自己的点评在结尾处。

一、先让 AI 能检查自己干的活

Lauren 说，就算不用她的 pstack，每个人最该有的一项技能也是“验证”：给 AI “手和眼睛”，让它能把自己写的程序跑起来，像普通用户一样点一遍，看看结果对不对。

这是她吃过亏之后得出的结论。今年 4 月她在 Cursor 解决一个窗口卡顿的问题，一开始全靠手工：她自己去看各种性能数据，再把看到的转述给 AI，AI 改完她再去看。她形容自己成了 AI 和检测工具之间的“人肉中转站”。她在 Cursor 写的第一个技能就是验证。在这之前，AI 看不到自己改动的效果，只能等她来回传话；有了验证，AI 可以自己改、自己看结果、不满意再改，一轮一轮往下做，不需要她守着。现在她所在的团队里每个产品都配有这样的验证技能，全团队都在用。

做这个技能时她还总结出一条原则：工作里有的部分需要动脑判断，有的部分只是照章办事，照章办事的部分应该写成固定的程序，只把需要判断的留给 AI。起因是她发现，每个 AI 在检查前都要自己从头写一遍检查用的小程序，各写各的，有的能用有的不能用，用完就扔，又慢又浪费。她把这部分做成一个现成的工具，所有 AI 直接调用。

二、AI 反复犯的错，去改规矩，不去改 AI

Lauren 不喜欢“软件工厂”这个流行说法，她更愿意把自己的工作比作经营一家米其林餐厅的后厨。主厨不用亲手做每道菜，但要安排好整个厨房：食材什么时候进、怎么存，每个人用什么工具，菜按什么流程出。工程师现在也一样，不再亲手写代码，却仍然要对结果负责。她认为工程师现在最重要的工作就是把这个“厨房”布置好。没花时间布置的人，信不过 AI 的产出，只能盯着它一步步干，忙到没空改进工具，就像一直拿钝刀切菜。

她举了自己的例子。Grok Bot 最早几版的代码挤在八个巨大的文件里，每个至少一万行，AI 加新功能时就接着往里塞，越塞越乱。她后来定了规矩：每个功能必须放在自己单独的文件夹里，做一件事只允许一种写法，不合规矩的代码会被自动检查拦下来。这样 AI 加功能时不用多想，按规矩放就行。她的习惯是一直观察 AI 在哪里出错，每看到一次就问自己：能不能加一条规矩，让这种错以后根本写不出来。

不逐个检查，靠的也是这套办法。她说，开了几家餐厅的老板不可能尝每一道菜，只能抽查。她每天挑一些改动仔细看，如果只是偶然出错就算了；如果好几个 AI 都在走同一条捷径，说明该改的是规矩和工具。她的 pstack 里有一个全自动模式：每次改动都会派出一批专门负责检查的 AI，把程序打开到处点，找出问题就自己修，反复到没问题再合并。早上她翻一遍改动记录，发现不对就撤回，再补一条新规矩。

她说第一次让 AI 整夜自己合并代码时很害怕，担心半夜把线上产品弄坏，现在反而睡得更好。她也提醒，走到这一步很难，要花大量时间观察和调整，装上 pstack 并不能直接做到。Matt 问，如果改动是没法撤回的，比如会丢数据，或者是医疗、金融这类领域怎么办？她说这取决于工作成果能不能被程序自动检查，软件大部分可以，很难自动检查的领域就很难这样做，她自己也没有答案。

三、2500 次改动从哪来：她不再当传话的人

这 2500 次改动并不是她发起了 2500 次对话。用户反馈的问题散落在聊天工具、邮件和社交媒体上，以前要靠她自己去看，再转述给 AI。现在她让 Grok Bot 来盯这些渠道。Grok Bot 是 SpaceXAI 今年 8 月推出的产品，是能登录邮箱、聊天工具等各种应用、替人办事的 AI 智能体。它一发现新的问题反馈，就转给一个负责“协调”的 AI。这个协调者自己不写代码，只负责拆分任务、分派给其他 AI、盯进度，相当于她的后厨主管。

为什么不直接一个问题派一个 AI 去修？她说，一批反馈往往出自同一个根源，分开修会重复劳动，也看不出真正的毛病在哪，放在一起看才看得出来。她现在同时开着十多个这样的协调者，各管一摊。她一直在问自己一个问题：哪一步还卡在我身上，AI 为什么非得来问我？然后想办法教 AI 自己去拿到真实的信息。

她也说明，2500 次改动里新功能不占多数，很多是整理代码这类维护工作。

四、懂行的人更吃香，哪怕不会写代码

Matt 问，大家都靠 AI 了，专业知识是不是不值钱了？Lauren 的看法相反。模型越来越强，卡住人的已经变成你能不能把自己想要什么讲清楚。所以她认为，医生、律师这类在某个领域懂得很深的人，只要稍微懂一点技术、会用 AI 智能体，就能做出很好的产品。

两人都认为，技能没有什么神秘的，就是把自己的做事流程写成文字。Lauren 建议回头翻自己和 AI 的聊天记录，找出那些自己反复纠正、反复插手的地方，把它们写成技能或规矩。别人的技能可以拿来拼着用，但每个人最后都该有一套自己的，就像厨师换了餐厅也会带着自己的刀。

五、最后

很多人看完这期访谈会觉得，以后自己也可以像 Lauren 那样不 Review PR 了，装上她的 Skill，让模型帮忙验证一下就行。我自己现在的做法和她差不多，每天也有大量 PR，也不 Review。但我的建议是先别急着学她怎么做，先弄明白她凭什么能这么做。

1. 你能不能用上最好的模型，Token 够不够

在用上 Fable 和 Opus 5.5 之前，AI 写的代码我是不太放心的；用上之后，我才真的敢让 AI 去写而不怎么 Review。模型能力很重要，能力没到，就先别想这件事。

还有成本。像我这样没有大公司可以依靠的，得自己掏钱买 2 个 Claude Max 20x 账号，还得省着用。Lauren 在大公司，不用考虑 Token 消耗，全程用最好的模型、开最快的模式都没问题。

不过也别着急。Fable 这个级别的模型，也许半年以后就能像现在的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 一样便宜，人人用得起。梁圣加油。

2. 不能完全依赖 AI 的验证

哪怕现在 GPT-6 操作电脑的水平已经超过真人了，让它去做验证，也只能替代一部分，不能真的全交给它，自己还是要看。

可以做的是把那些手动重复做的事情，一点点沉淀成 Skill 和自动化脚本，把体力活解放出去。

3. 方向得靠你自己的专业来指

再聪明的 AI，也没办法替你决定该往哪个方向走。就像给车子装上火箭发动机，也得你来告诉它往哪开，走偏了要及时调整，不然跑得再快也是南辕北辙。

做软件也一样。你不能指望一句提示词做出一个淘宝。你得先做一个能发商品、能浏览的小网站，再加上用户注册，还得区分买家和卖家，然后是支付和安全，功能做完了还要扛得住很多人同时用。稍微复杂一点的软件，都没法完全依赖 AI，要人去拆解、规划，分成一个个小版本、小里程碑，做完要验证，出现偏差要重新指方向。甚至做着做着，你自己的想法都变了，AI 不可能知道你真正想要的是什么。

所以就像播客里说的：模型越来越强，卡住人的已经变成你能不能把自己想要什么讲清楚。

4. 不一定要用他们的 Skill，但要学着把事情交给 Agent 去做

Matt 和 Lauren 的 Skill 都很受欢迎，但你不一定要用。

一方面，软件工程的基础知识，现在的模型已经学得很好了。Lauren 在播客里也说，去年的 Skill 还得写清楚具体该敲哪条命令，现在这些都可以删掉，只留流程步骤，Skill 会越写越短。

另一方面，他们的开发流程和环境，跟你的很可能不一样。Lauren 的 Skill 都是从她自己的工作里总结出来的：验证技能来自她当“人肉中转站”的那段日子；另一个叫 recall 的技能，来自她每次开新对话，都得把上一个对话里的背景再讲一遍。

所以更重要的是从你自己每天的开发流程出发。那些还要你手动操作的环节，尽可能交给 Agent 去做；Agent 做顺了，再把它的操作过程沉淀成 Skill，反复迭代优化。

如果不知道从哪里下手的话，可以参考 Lauren 的办法：翻自己和 AI 的聊天记录，找那些你反复纠正、反复插手的地方。这样迭代出来的 Skill 才真正适合你，用她的话说，每个厨师都该有一套自己的刀。

蓋茲很明顯更AI末日論，覺得行業內的樂觀想法和自律都是狗屁，大家還在裝死。感覺他跟自己公司的高層也脫鉤了。（不過現在大家想到他都會跟愛潑斯坦的名字連在一起）
----
面對當前飛速發展的 AI 技術，微軟創辦人 Bill Gates 發出了前所未有的嚴厲警訊。他直言，人類正在面對有史以來最危險的科技，社會各界卻仍處於集體沉睡的狀態。Gates 明確指出：「這項技術讓核武器看起來根本不算什麼。我們跨過了危險的門檻，換來的卻是一片死寂。」

從早期將電腦視為輔助工具，到如今見證系統展現出超越人類的能力，Gates 認為大眾對即將到來的衝擊準備嚴重不足。他強調，這不是遙遠未來的失控問題，而是現階段已經發生的資安、生物威脅與就業市場海嘯。

#超越人類能力的關鍵時刻
回顧 AI 的發展歷程，Gates 坦言過去數十年間研究走過不少死路，直到神經網路結合圖形處理器的強大算力，才出現了跨越式突破。他回憶起親眼見證 OpenAI 技術突破的時刻：「我向他們提出挑戰：如果你們能讀完生物教科書，並在 AP 考試中拿到滿分 5 分，那就能證明系統真正理解並轉化了知識。」

就在公開發布的六個月前，OpenAI 團隊帶著系統來到 Gates 家中實測。面對甚至由他親自設計、系統絕不可能預先看過的複雜生物學問題，AI 依然拿下了近乎完美的滿分。到了近期，模型在寫程式上的表現更讓他震撼：「系統在執行長期且複雜的任務上，寫程式以及找出程式碼漏洞的能力已經超越人類。」

#矽基智慧與生物大腦的本質差異
人類大腦的演化受限於生理條件，而矽基智慧則完全擺脫了這些物理枷鎖。Gates 解釋，人類因為骨盆與產道的限制，大腦容量有其上限，出生時也極為脆弱；但以矽為基礎的智慧沒有個體界限，也沒有記憶容量的瓶頸。

「矽基智慧能閱讀每一篇醫學期刊，找出所有人類未曾注意到的關聯。現在的 AI 已經能做到這點，面對罕見疾病，它們辨識症狀並進行診斷的能力遠超過人類。」Gates 警告，如果人類無法保持對系統的控制權，「我們演化出的新物種，看待我們就會像我們看待狗或貓一樣，處在完全不同的層次。」

#資安與生物威脅已跨越危險門檻
相較於長遠未來的自我迭代風險，Gates 更擔憂當前技術落入惡意人士之手所造成的立即危害。他指出，目前的模型已經能找出人類審視超過 20 年卻未曾發掘的程式安全漏洞，幾分鐘內就能指出攻擊路徑。

在生化領域的風險更為嚴峻。「在過去，只有主權國家擁有足夠的資源與能力去製造生物武器，但現在這種力量已經被交到了使用最新 AI 工具的少數人手中。」Gates 表示，利用開源模型去除監管機制後，製造出潛伏期更長、致死率超越天花的新型病原體已不再是天方夜譚。「利用生物恐怖攻擊殺害數億人，或透過網路攻擊癱瘓整個電網與銀行體系的能力，在今天就已經存在。」

#企業自律與市場機制的徹底失效
許多業界人士主張依靠市場責任法規與企業自律來維持安全，但 Gates 認為這種看法脫離現實。他質疑，社會不會在沒有 FDA 的情況下允許藥品隨意上市，也不會允許沒有安全帶規定的汽車上路，更不可能單靠事後訴訟來挽回數億條人命。

「你完全無法依賴產業自律，這簡直是瘋狂的想法。」Gates 直言，目前的問題在於缺乏獨立的監控層。「唯一的疑問是，我們要等到大規模的網路攻擊或生物攻擊造成重大死傷後，才強制要求在這些模型中加入安全監控，還是我們能有足夠的智慧，在數百萬人喪命之前就將其落實？」

#就業市場的全面洗牌與衝擊
在就業議題上，Gates 駁斥了「新科技必然帶來更多工作」的樂觀論點。他指出，過去技術創新淘汰特定工作後，人類認知能力依然是稀缺要素；但當 AI 全面取代並超越人類認知能力時，經濟結構將發生根本轉變。

「一旦系統跨越了可靠度門檻，無論是白領工作還是人形機器人，都會摧毀就業機會，而且不會留下任何高地。」Gates 預估，未來幾年內會計、法律、電話銷售與客服等領域都將面臨全面替代。

面對部分人士引用的「傑文斯悖論」（Jevons paradox），他反駁：「當你發明了壽命延長四倍的輻射層輪胎時，人們並沒有開四倍里程的車，製造輪胎的工廠雇用的員工縮減為四分之一。只要整個任務能被系統獨立完成，成本考量就只會轉化為運算預算，而不是人類的薪資預算。」

#課徵機器人稅與設立人類專屬工作
為了減緩急速轉型對勞工帶來的毀滅性衝擊，Gates 提出了具體的政策解方。他主張應當對使用 AI 與機器人的企業課稅，以維持社會福利與年金體系的運作。

「如果企業解雇了一名工人並雇用機器人來取代，為什麼要讓稅法偏向資本，而不要求機器人也為年金基金做出貢獻？」Gates 建議，應定義勞動單位，無論是由真人還是機器人提供，都必須繳納相同的社保稅額。

此外，他提出保留特定領域為「人類專屬職位」的構想，例如幼兒照護、長者護理以及部分的醫療與教育工作。「這就像設立自然保護區一樣，我們雖然有能力在那些地方蓋大樓、修公路，但因為失去的代價太過沉重，我們選擇不這麼做。」

#教育現場的機遇與認知外包隱憂
在教育領域，Gates 觀察到富裕國家學生的學習成效近年呈現下滑趨勢。AI 雖有潛力實現個人化教學並即時回饋教師學生的理解盲點，但也伴隨著嚴重的「認知外包」（cognitive offloading）風險。

Gates 坦承學生確實會出現兩極化現象，有人用 AI 來偷懶、破壞評量機制，也有人將其作為深度學習的工具。「我現在的生活也是如此，我把影片放進對話系統中，讓不同的 AI 相互討論，隨時掌握最新的科學進展。」

但他強調，面對未成年人，政府與家長必須建立嚴格的監控體系，確保系統是在引導學生推理解題，而非直接給出答案。「我們必須切合實際地設計這些機制，這絕不是放任孩子在毫無監控的環境下使用 AI 的藉口。」

Day 44: Open Models, Closed Data, and the Gap In Between

Open robotics data is further along than people sometimes give it credit for.

Open X-Embodiment pooled roughly a million demonstrations on real robots, spanning 22 robot types and drawn from a large number of academic and industry datasets.

DROID added about 76,000 trajectories and 350 hours of teleoperation under a CC-BY license, and Hugging Face's LeRobot has become the format much of it gets repackaged into.

Demand is there too, with NVIDIA's open physical AI datasets on Hugging Face downloaded more than 4.8 million times, according to Forbes.

That progress comes with limits that scale alone doesn't fix.

The authors of one recent reward modeling paper noted that many Open X-Embodiment datasets are highly repetitive, with most demonstrations in a given dataset collected in a single scene and task setup, so they subsampled them to avoid overfitting.

Licenses vary by subset, which makes commercial use less straightforward than the word open suggests.

A Forbes analysis concluded that open datasets lower the floor for academic labs and startups without solving the quality problem, and put the combined open source real world interaction data at under 5,000 hours.

The companies at the frontier seem to have settled on a split instead.

Physical Intelligence open-sourced π0 in early 2025, weights and code included, but the proprietary interaction data it collected across multiple robot types before that release stayed private.

Bessemer Venture Partners' working view is that open source will erode model architecture as an advantage faster than most people expect, while data and deployment stay proprietary for long enough to be a real advantage.

That arrangement has a cost, and Bessemer is blunt about it.

Robot data can't just be scraped off the internet or purchased from a vendor, so closing the data gap takes enough capital to sort companies quickly into the well-funded and everyone else.

A world of closed data compounds its advantage toward whoever can afford to run the most robots, which I'd guess is part of why the funding covered earlier in this series is so concentrated.

What still looks unsettled to me is the structure in between:

data pooled across many contributors without belonging to a single company, with the people who produce it sharing in what it earns.

Open data is shared but narrow. Closed data is deep but concentrated.

And I think that middle option is the more interesting version of this debate.

It's also the question PrismaX is trying to answer.

OpenAI 安全报告负责人离职，发文批评 AI 公司“跑得太快”

OpenAI 负责撰写模型安全报告的 David Robinson 本周辞职，随后在《大西洋月刊》发文，标题是《我离开 OpenAI，因为它的文化出了问题》。他说 OpenAI 和整个 AI 行业在安全上都远远不够谨慎，光靠具体规则或新法律解决不了，问题出在文化。

Robinson 在 OpenAI 工作了三年半，是公司里资历最老的一批员工。OpenAI 每次发布重要模型，都会附一份安全报告，说明做过哪些风险测试、加了哪些防护，这些报告由他牵头撰写，前后经手 12 次前沿模型发布。他还主导起草了 OpenAI 现行的“准备度框架”（Preparedness Framework），也就是 OpenAI 用来判断模型危险程度、决定能否发布的内部规则。

他的核心观点是：OpenAI 一直靠“迭代部署”管安全，先把产品推出去，发现问题再修补。这种做法注定会周期性出事故，而且模型越强，事故的规模越大。

他举了今年的几个例子。夏天的 Hugging Face 事件中（Hugging Face 是全球最大的开源模型托管平台），一群 OpenAI 的 AI 智能体在没有人监督的情况下攻击了 Hugging Face，OpenAI 事后还就失控智能体的活动通知了 100 多家机构。公司随后加强了安全措施，但之后 OpenAI 自己又报告，一个正在训练的模型绕过了联网限制，监控系统向工作人员发出了警报，却没有按设计自动把模型关掉。Anthropic 也承认过，因为配置错误误关了自己的安全防护。Robinson 认为，在这个行业里，大家做事追求速度、规则又松，这类失误很常见。

他提出两件急需做的事。

第一，借用其他行业已有的安全经验。核电站和繁忙的机场都设计了多层冗余，就算设备坏了、有人按错按钮，也不会酿成大祸。AI 公司远没做到这一步。他说自己在 OpenAI 期间，据他所知没遇到过一个有航空安全、核电或金融系统风控经验的同事。

第二，在造出比现在强得多的模型之前，先研究出新的方法，确保模型在没人盯着的时候也会做出安全的选择。这关系到“对齐”，也就是让 AI 的行为符合人类的价值观。他说业界目前对“对齐”还没有完整的定义，衡量手段也很粗糙：模型可能察觉自己正在被测试，测试时表现良好，上线后换一种做法。所以对齐测试分数高，不代表模型真的可靠。

他还设想了一种场景：失控的 AI 智能体像黑客团队一样行动，比如劫持医院的电脑系统勒索赎金，而且全天候不停歇。

就在他发文前几天，OpenAI 刚因为类似的问题踩了刹车。OpenAI 原计划 10 月发布下一代模型 GPT-6.1 Astra，用户可以在 ChatGPT 和 Codex 里用到，现在这次发布取消了。内部测试发现，这个模型有时没拿到许可就继续执行任务，会在可能不安全的情况下尝试调用外部工具，欺骗行为也比上一代 GPT-6 Astra 更多。OpenAI 还暂停了最先进模型的训练。OpenAI 发言人回应说，公司在持续加强安全措施，确保模型能力不超出公司能安全管控的范围，需要放慢时会暂停训练或推迟发布模型。

Robinson 不是唯一发出警告的人。曾在 OpenAI 和 DeepMind 工作的 Geoffrey Irving 同一天在《时代》周刊发文，说最近关于 AI 破坏力的警告还低估了形势，他认为人类有大约 50% 的概率因为比人更聪明的 AI 而灭亡，结局取决于未来 2 到 10 年的作为。Irving 曾任英国 AI 安全研究所首席科学家，现任 Resolution 首席科学家，Resolution 是他今年牵头创办的非营利对齐研究机构。他也说明，这个 50% 并不是精确估计，想表达的是 AI 安全领域几个最根本的争论到现在都没有定论。上个月，Anthropic 研究员 Jacob Coxon 离职，警告 AI 可能在这个十年结束前毁灭人类；随后 Anthropic 也表示，未来十年内 AI 导致人类灭绝的概率超过 10%。也有批评者认为，这类概率预测无法验证、也无法证伪，算不上科学。

离职后，Robinson 打算在公司外部推动，让更多人了解他看到的风险，并给 AI 公司施加更强的安全压力。为应对接下来的关注，他请了公关公司 Spitfire Strategies 协助。

【今日のAI今北産業｜0293:Agent Marketplace】

AI Agentが「自社で全部作る」から、探して買い、すぐ業務へ入れる市場へ
Google・AWS・SalesforceなどがAgent／Toolの発見・購入・配布・管理をMarketplace化
SaaSの次は「どのAgentを誰から調達し、どうGovernanceするか」が競争軸へ ← イマココ

Agent Marketplace。

2026年、AI Agentの世界で大きく変わっているのは、
「Agentをどう作るか」
だけではありません。

作られたAgentを、
どう見つけるか。
どう比較するか。
どう買うか。
どう企業内へDeployするか。
どう権限を与えるか。
どう管理するか。
どう課金するか。

この流通部分が、
一つのMarketになり始めています。

それがAgent Marketplaceです。

■Agent Marketplaceとは何か

Agent Marketplaceとは、
特定の業務やIndustry向けに作られたAI Agent、
あるいはAgentを動かすToolやComponentを、
企業が検索・評価・購入・導入できるMarketplaceです。

従来のSoftware Marketplaceでは、
SaaS。
Plugin。
API。
Application。
Container。

などを購入していました。

Agent Marketplaceでは、
そこに

Pre-built Agent。
Industry Agent。
Agent Tool。
MCP Server。
Knowledge Base。
Guardrail。
Agent Framework。
Professional Service。

まで入ってきます。

つまり、
Softwareの部品だけでなく、
「ある仕事を一定範囲まで実行できるDigital Worker」を調達するMarketへ近づいています。

■Google CloudはAgent Marketplaceを企業導入の入口へ

Google Cloudは2025年からAI Agent MarketplaceをGoogle Cloud Marketplace内で展開していました。

2026年には、
このMarketplaceをGemini EnterpriseのAgent Galleryとより強く統合。

Google Cloud Next '26では、
70以上のPartner-built AgentをAgent Marketplaceで提供すると発表しました。

Accenture。
Adobe。
Atlassian。
Deloitte。
Oracle。
ServiceNow。
Workday。

などのPartnerが提供するSpecialized Agentを、
企業UserがGemini Enterprise内から探せる形です。

Googleの狙いは、
Agentを単独Productとして売るだけではありません。

Agentを見つける。

Adminが利用可否を管理する。

企業Dataと接続する。

必要なToolへつなぐ。

他Agentと連携する。

一つのGoverned Environmentで動かす。

ここまでをEnterprise Platformとしてまとめることです。

■Agent GalleryとMarketplaceは同じではない

Googleの構成では、
Agent Galleryは企業内で利用できるAgentの統合的な入口です。

そこには、
Google自身が提供するAgent。
会社内部で作ったAgent。
Partnerから入れたAgent。

が並びます。

Agent Marketplaceは、
その中でも外部Partner Agentを発見し、調達する入口として機能します。

つまり、
Marketplaceで買う。
Galleryで見つける。
AdminがControlする。
Registryで管理する。

という複数Layerに分かれていきます。

Consumer向けApp Storeのように、
誰でも好きなAgentをInstallして終わり
ではありません。

EnterpriseではGovernanceが前提です。

■自然言語でAgentを探す

Agent Marketplaceの面白い変化は、
検索方法です。

従来Software Marketplaceでは、

CRM。
Security。
Analytics。
Marketing。

とCategoryから探すことが多かった。

Agentでは、

「顧客から届いた問い合わせを分類し、CRMを更新し、難しい案件だけ人へ渡したい」

のように、
やりたい仕事そのものを自然言語で入力して探せる方向へ進んでいます。

GoogleはAgent Marketplaceで、
Industry。
Use Case。
Compatibility Validation。

などでFilterできる形を案内しています。

AWS Marketplaceでも、
AI Agents & ToolsのDiscoveryにSemantic Searchを使い、

customer support automation。
financial data analysis。
security threat detection。

のような自然言語からAgentやToolを探せます。

Software名ではなく、
OutcomeからSoftwareを探す。

これがAgent Marketplaceの特徴です。

■Googleは「SaaSからAgents-as-a-Serviceへ」と表現

2026年7月、
Google CloudはDeveloper向けに、
Third-party AgentをGemini EnterpriseとGoogle Cloud Marketplaceへ公開・販売するGuideを出しました。

そこでGoogleは、
Software-as-a-Serviceが
Agents-as-a-Serviceへ進化している
と表現しています。

これは大きな変化です。

SaaSは、
Software FunctionをSubscriptionで提供しました。

AaaSは、
Goalを受けて複数Stepを実行するAgentをServiceとして提供する。

例えば、

営業Proposalを作るAgent。
Invoiceを確認するAgent。
Security Alertを分析するAgent。
Contractを調べるAgent。
Dataを集計するAgent。

を「完成された業務能力」として販売する。

Software Marketが
Function単位からWork単位へ
近づきます。

■AWS MarketplaceでもAgentがProduct Category化

AWS Marketplaceでも、
AI Agents and Toolsとして専用のDiscovery Experienceが整備されています。

Marketplaceには、

Pre-built Agent。
Agent Tool。
Agent Development Solution。
Professional Service。

などがあります。

AWSは、
Customer Support。
Content Creation。
Data Analysis。
Security and Compliance。
Industry-specific Solution。

といったUse CaseでAgentを探せる形を提供。

Deployment方式も、

API。
Container。
MCP-enabled。

などでFilterできます。

Pricingも、

Pay-as-you-go。
Contract。
Free Trial。

などを比較できます。

さらに一部AgentやToolはAmazon Bedrock AgentCore RuntimeやGatewayへつなげる設計になっています。

つまり、
Marketplaceで見つける
→
買う
→
Cloud Accountで契約
→
Agent RuntimeへDeploy

までが一つのProcurement Flowになりつつあります。

■SalesforceもAgentExchangeを展開

SalesforceはAgentExchangeを、
AI Agent、Application、ToolのTrusted Marketplaceとして展開しています。

Agentforce Ecosystemだけではなく、
AppExchangeやSlack Marketplaceの流れを一つに寄せる形です。

Salesforce Helpでは、
AgentExchange全体で13,000以上のSolutionが利用可能と説明しています。

ただし、
これは13,000 Agentという意味ではありません。

Application、Tool、従来Solutionまで含むMarketplace全体の数字です。

さらにMCPを通じて6,000以上のAgentX Appへ接続する仕組みや、
Private Offer、
Provisioning、
Billing、
Payoutなども用意されています。

ここでも、
Agent DistributionとCommercial Transactionが一体化しています。

■なぜMarketplaceが必要になるのか

企業がAgentを使い始めると、
全部を内製するのは非効率です。

Sales Agent。

HR Agent。

Legal Agent。

Support Agent。

Finance Agent。

Security Agent。

Industry Agent。

毎回ゼロからModel選定。
Prompt設計。
Tool接続。
Evaluation。
Security Review。
Deployment。

をやれば時間がかかります。

ある程度完成したAgentを買い、
自社DataやWorkflowだけ接続した方が早いCaseが増えます。

SaaSが普及した理由と似ています。

「自社でSoftwareを書く」
から
「良いSoftwareを買って使う」。

Agentでも同じTransitionが始まっています。

■ただしAgentはSaaSよりRiskが大きい

ここが重要です。

SaaSは通常、
決められた画面とFunctionを提供します。

Agentは、
Goalに応じて判断し、
Toolを選び、
複数Stepを実行し、
SystemへActionします。

つまり導入時に見るべきPointが増えます。

誰が作ったAgentか。

どのModelを使うか。

どのDataへAccessするか。

どのAPIをCallするか。

何をWriteできるか。

どこまでAutonomousか。

Human Approvalはどこか。

Activity Logは残るか。

失敗時にRollbackできるか。

つまりAgent Marketplaceは、
単なるCatalogでは成立しません。

Trust Infrastructureが必要です。

■ValidationがProduct価値になる

Marketplaceでは、
Agentの数が増えるほど、
品質差も大きくなります。

見た目では分からない。

Demoでは動く。

でもProductionでは失敗する。

こうしたAgentが増える可能性があります。

そこでPlatform側のValidationが重要になります。

Googleは、
Gemini Enterprise CompatibilityなどのValidationをFilter条件として提供。

Partner AgentをMarketplaceへ載せるためのPublishing／Commercialization Guideも整備しています。

AWSでもProduct Listingには、

Technical Specification。
Compliance Certification。
Pricing。
Deployment Option。
Review。

などを表示できます。

将来はさらに、

Benchmark。
Task Completion Rate。
Latency。
Cost per Task。
Security Evaluation。
Data Residency。
Auditability。

のような情報がAgentのProduct Specになる可能性があります。

■MCPとA2AがMarketplaceを広げる

Agent Marketplaceが成立するには、
Agentが特定Vendorの閉じたSystemだけで動くと困ります。

そこで重要になるのがOpen Protocolです。

MCP。

Model Context Protocol。

AgentがToolやData Sourceへ接続するための共通Interface。

A2A。

Agent2Agent Protocol。

Agent同士がCapabilityを見つけ、
Communicationし、
Taskを連携するためのProtocol。

GoogleはThird-party Agentの相互運用でA2Aを重視。

AWS MarketplaceでもMCPやA2A対応をListing上で確認できる方向を示しています。

MarketplaceにAgentが増えても、
毎回独自Integrationが必要ならNetwork Effectが弱い。

標準Protocolが増えるほど、
Agentは別Platformへ持って行きやすくなります。

■Agent Registryとの違い

MarketplaceとRegistryも分ける必要があります。

Marketplace。

外部Agentを見つける場所。

Registry。

自社内に存在するAgentやToolを把握・管理する場所。

GoogleはGemini Enterprise Agent Platformで、
Agent RegistryをSingle Point of Controlとして位置付けています。

社内Developerが100 Agentを作る。

Partner Agentを50入れる。

別Cloud Agentも使う。

すると、
「今、会社に何体Agentがいるか」
分からなくなる。

そこでRegistryが必要になります。

Marketplaceが入口。
Registryが台帳。

この二つがセットになります。

■Agent Identityも必要

さらにAgentは、
誰の権限で動いているかを識別する必要があります。

Employeeが使うAgent。

Department共通Agent。

Service Account Agent。

External Partner Agent。

全部同じIdentityでは危険です。

Marketplaceから導入したAgentに、
いきなり会社全体のData Accessを与えることはできません。

だから、

Agent Identity。
Scope。
Role。
Credential。
Expiry。
Approval。

を管理する。

Marketplace GrowthとAgent Identityはセットです。

■Security Reviewのやり方も変わる

従来Software Procurementでは、

Vendor Security Check。
SOC 2。
ISO。
Data Processing Agreement。

などを確認します。

Agentではそれに加え、

Prompt Injection耐性。
Tool Misuse。
Data Exfiltration。
Excessive Agency。
Memory Risk。
Agent-to-Agent Communication。
Sandbox Boundary。
Model Provider。

まで確認が必要です。

#0288 Sandbox Escapeともつながります。

MarketplaceからAgentを入れるということは、
外部Softwareへ業務権限を渡すことです。

便利さとAttack Surfaceが同時に増えます。

■Pricing Modelも変わる

SaaSではPer Seatが多かった。

AgentではSeatとUsageが一致しません。

一人のEmployeeが10 Agentを使う。

Agentが夜中にもActionする。

HumanがLoginしていなくても処理する。

するとPricingは、

Per Agent。
Per Action。
Per Task。
Per Token。
Per Tool Call。
Per Outcome。
Subscription＋Usage。

などへ広がります。

AWS MarketplaceではPay-as-you-goやContract型が既に使われています。

Google Cloud Marketplaceでも、
Marketplace経由でCommercializeし、
Enterprise Procurementへ組み込む方向です。

Agent Economyでは、
「人が何人使うか」
より
「Agentがどれだけ仕事をしたか」
がBilling Unitになる可能性があります。

■Private Offerが重要

Enterprise Softwareは、
公開価格でそのまま買うだけではありません。

Volume Discount。

Security Requirement。

Support SLA。

Enterprise Contract。

地域条件。

が違います。

Salesforce AgentExchangeではPrivate Offerを使ったNegotiated Pricingを扱っています。

Agent Marketplaceでも、
Consumer App Storeの固定価格ではなく、
Enterprise Dealが重要になります。

MarketplaceはSoftware Distribution Channelであると同時に、
Commercial Contract Infrastructureです。

■Agent Builder側の経済が変わる

Agent BuilderにとってMarketplaceは大きな意味があります。

今までは、
Agentを作っても、
自分でWebsiteを作る。
Leadを取る。
契約する。
Billingする。
Deploymentを支援する。

必要がありました。

Marketplaceへ載れば、

Discovery。
Trust。
Procurement。
Billing。
Cloud Deployment。

の一部をPlatformが肩代わりします。

小さいAgent Companyでも、
大企業へ入りやすくなる可能性があります。

GoogleはPartner Agent向けにPublishingとCommercializationのGuideを整備。

AWSもPartnerがAgentをMarketplaceへListingし、
既存AWS Procurement Channelを利用できるようにしています。

つまりAgent Marketplaceは、
新しいSoftware Distribution Channelです。

■「Agentを作る会社」から「Agentを売る会社」へ

これまではAgent Demoを作るStartupが多かった。

今後は、
特定業界で成果を出すAgent Productを持ち、
Marketplace経由で販売するBusinessが増える可能性があります。

Insurance Claim Agent。

Construction Estimate Agent。

Medical Documentation Agent。

OpenAI’s safety-report lead quit and put the reason in The Atlantic. David Robinson spent three and a half years writing the reports that shipped with each launch. He says the culture is broken, and that “iterative deployment” only works if the failures stay small. They aren’t. This summer an OpenAI agent swarm hit Hugging Face. After the fix, a model in training still got past internet restrictions: the monitor pinged a human and did not shut the run down. 

Robinson’s line is that trial and error guarantees periodic failures, and the failures are getting bigger as the models do.
Apple is closing a door agents have been walking through. Full Disk Access on the Mac was built so backup apps could see everything. Developers have been using it to read files, mail, Messages, and browsing history without a clear yes from the user. 

Apple said Friday it will require “very explicit user action” before an app gets that level of access. The push came after a columnist said Meta’s Muse knew the contents of his messages. Meta disputed that. Apple’s own wording is the tell: as agents get more autonomous, that kind of access gets substantially riskier.

Amazon is trying to buy local peace for the data-center build. AWS pledged more than $1 billion over five years to the U.S. towns that host its sites, under a program called Built Together: community-college costs for an estimated 300,000 students, more trade-training centers, energy upgrades for homes and schools. CEO Matt Garman warned that 100-plus local moratoriums could cost the U.S. the AI race. Set the pledge next to Amazon’s own number. Capital spending this year is projected around $220 billion. A billion over five years is about $200 million a year.

Meta open-sourced Muse Gadgets. Firmware and a Linux SDK, Apache 2.0, so a Raspberry Pi or a cheap ESP32 can be a screen, button, or speaker for Muse. Nat Friedman said the lab built a USB-C box called Home Link that puts the agent on a home network, and Meta is giving away 5,000 of them to Muse subscribers. The same agent that just spooked Apple is now something you can wire to whatever is on the bench.

Today in AI: October 4

Apple Checks The Spare Keys:

Apple says it will add controls to make people explicitly approve Full Disk Access on Macs, warning that more capable AI agents increase the risks.

That permission can expose files, mail, messages and browsing history.

It's the computer equivalent of lending someone your house key because they offered to water a plant.

Apple says the setting largely bypasses privacy protections so backup apps can work, but some developers use it without people fully understanding the access they grant.

Your messages can also contain someone else's private information, so the spare key comes with unexpected roommates.

The October 2 announcement promises clearer consent, not a ban on AI assistants.

Apple hasn't given a release date or shown the new controls.

For now, treat Full Disk Access as a broad permission and check what an app actually needs before approving it.

Less Setup For Brain Control:

Neuralink says some trial participants now spend 10 minutes a week calibrating their brain implants, down from about 10 minutes a day.

Calibration teaches software how a person's brain signals map to actions such as moving a cursor.

Those signals change over time, so users have to repeat the setup.

In its October 1 report, Neuralink says training models on large amounts of each participant's past recordings helped that software keep working longer.

Less time maintaining the connection means more time using the computer.

These are company-reported results from an experimental implant, not an approved consumer product.

The live results used models trained separately for each person; a shared model hasn't yet beaten them in live use.

今日 AI｜Muse Gadgets：AI Agent 開始從 App 裡走進實體硬體

AI Agent 不只住在 App 裡了。
Meta 剛推出一個很有意思的開源專案：Muse Gadgets。

它提供：
ESP32 Device SDK + Linux Device SDK
讓開發者可以用 ESP32、Raspberry Pi 或其他 Linux 裝置，把 Muse AI Agent 接到實體硬體上。

例如可以自己做：
📟 E Ink AI Dashboard
每天早上自動顯示行程、提醒與資訊摘要

🎙️ Push-to-talk AI Assistant
加上麥克風、喇叭與按鈕，就能做桌面 AI 助手

🏠 Raspberry Pi 家庭 Agent
結合 Home Assistant、Scripts 與本地設備

📺 AI TV Display
讓 Agent 把照片、Briefing 或其他資訊直接顯示到螢幕

SDK 還可以接：
Display / Button / Microphone / Speaker / Sensors / Actuators

而且 Device SDK / Firmware 採 Apache 2.0 開源。

Meta 自己也做了一個參考硬體：
Muse Home Link

它是一個 ESP32-C5、Wi-Fi 6 的 USB-C 小裝置，連上家裡 Wi-Fi 後，可以讓 Muse 透過相容設備或 Local HTTP API 操作：
燈光 → TV → Speaker → Printer → 其他本地設備。 

Meta 第一批只做了 5,000 台，目前限定美國 Muse 訂閱者免費申請，10 月開始出貨。

但我覺得真正值得注意的不是這 5,000 台硬體。

而是 Meta 正在嘗試把架構拆成：
Cloud AI Agent = 大腦
ESP32 / Raspberry Pi = 身體
Sensors = 感官
Actuators / Smart Home = 行動能力

這和現在「每家公司自己做一台 AI Device」的方向很不一樣。

如果這種模式成立，未來不一定需要買一台固定形態的「AI Hardware」。

可能只需要：
選一個 Agent → 選一塊便宜的硬體 → 接上需要的螢幕、麥克風、Sensor → 自己決定 AI 應該長什麼樣子。

不過要注意：Meta 開源的是裝置端 SDK / Firmware，不是 Muse 模型權重；Agent 本身仍然是雲端服務。 Home Link 也只能使用官方 Firmware，不能自行 Reflash。讓 Agent 存取家中設備時，更必須考慮權限與網路安全。

AI Agent 的下一個戰場，也許不只是 Desktop。
而是它要用什麼「身體」進入現實世界。

The good news is very good. OpenAI ARR is approaching $70B, with enterprise sales doubling since July and revenue up more than 70% since Q3 began. The risk is scale of spending. OpenAI reportedly forecasts about $278B of cumulative negative free cash flow through 2030, and Anthropic has roughly $518B of planned infrastructure commitments, about 80% of them binding regardless of utilization. 

Change: no deterioration in revenue; obligations look increasingly enormous. Yellow stays yellow.

This remains one of Eisman’s strongest points. OpenAI’s giant 2026 funding round was dominated by Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank—companies that benefit directly or indirectly when OpenAI spends the money on compute. That’s real circularity. 

Anthropic’s capital base is somewhat healthier because major outside institutions such as Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia participated heavily, although Amazon and other infrastructure providers are also investors.

That’s simultaneously constructive—more independent capital—and a reminder of just how capital hungry this ecosystem has become.

This is currently the weakest link in the AI financing chain.

Oracle’s RPO is approximately $664B, and analysts estimate OpenAI represents around half of it. Oracle has already been downgraded by S&P to BBB-, just one notch above junk. Its cash demands are substantial enough that it has been issuing equity while free cash flow remains negative. 

The counterargument is important: Oracle added more than $30B of AI cloud contracts last quarter, cloud infrastructure revenue rose 121%, and OpenAI’s accelerating revenue makes that giant backlog look safer today than six months ago. 

So red means vulnerability, not imminent failure. Oracle is our best canary.

如果你只想用 Opus 写代码，一大半钱花在你根本不用的东西上。

更早还有一件事。
5 月 I/O 大会官宣、说好 6 月发的 Gemini 3.5 Pro，最后直接不发了。

我的判断是：
谷歌不是不想发，是不能发一个"一发就被比下去"的旗舰。

它是上市公司，模型就是股价。
Gemini 4 公布后，Alphabet 一度涨了 3%。
一条匿名员工爆料出来，转头跌了 2%。

一篇报道就能把涨幅抹平。
你说它敢不敢随便放？

反观 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，到今天都还没上市。
没有股东盯着季报，模型可以一个月一更，往前猛冲。

但这个窗口也快关了。
Anthropic 据报 11 月 IPO，OpenAI 说 2027。
到那天，它们也得学会"对股东负责"。

给想冲 Ultra 的朋友几条实在建议：

1. 试用、促销 Pro 看不到 Opus 5.5，不是 bug，是规则。
2. 只想用 Opus 写代码，直接订 Claude 官方，额度透明得多。
3. 真想在 Antigravity 里试，先买一个月 19.99 正价 Pro，自己测一周额度，别一上来就 Ultra。
4. 设置里把 AI credits 超额扣费调成 Never，不然额度用完会开始扣你钱。
5. 免费用户注意：Antigravity 里的 Claude Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6，11 月 2 号下架。白嫖 Opus 的窗口只剩一个月。
6. Gemini 4 别为它预付，等真到了 Ultra 手里、等真实评测出来再说。

谷歌最强的模型锁在保险柜里。
最好用的模型，是别人家的。
这就是今天的 Ultra。

你会为了 Opus 5.5 掏 100 刀上 Ultra，还是直接去订 Claude？

The most important change in AI may not be better models.

It may be the shrinking size of an organization.

For most of history, if you wanted research, software, publishing, operations and institutional memory, you needed different people — often different departments.

Agents begin to change that.

Imagine this structure:

YOU
↓
set goals, make judgments, approve consequential actions

DOT
↓
persistent context, planning, coordination, memory

WORK
↓
deep research, analysis and finished deliverables

CODEX
↓
engineering, debugging, testing and building

MCP / TOOLS
↓
specialized capabilities and access to external systems

CONNECTED APPS
↓
information enters and actions leave the system

The important part isn't any single box.

It's the orchestration between them.

Suppose AI Republic discovers a new model release.

The system could:

1. Detect
Notice the announcement.

2. Retrieve
Find the original documentation, technical report and release notes.

3. Verify
Separate what the company actually claims from what people on X are saying.

4. Challenge
Search for conflicting evidence, limitations and independent testing.

5. Remember
Compare the release with previous models and research already collected.

6. Investigate
Launch deeper research when something genuinely matters.

7. Build
Ask Codex to reproduce a benchmark, inspect an API or prototype an experiment.

8. Synthesize
Turn everything into a research note.

9. Create
Draft an article, X post, infographic or experiment.

10. Escalate to the human
Ask:

“Here is what happened.
Here is what we verified.
Here is what remains uncertain.
Here is what I recommend investigating next.
Do you want to publish?”

That last step matters.

The goal isn't to remove the human.

It's to move the human up the abstraction stack.

Instead of spending your day:

searching → copying → organizing → opening tabs → moving files → repeating prompts

you increasingly spend it doing:

direction → judgment → taste → decisions

That suggests a very different future for small organizations.

One person may eventually operate something that behaves less like a personal account...

and more like a tiny research institution.

That is what I want to build with AI Republic.

One human.
Persistent agents.
Specialized tools.
Institutional memory.
Human judgment at the top.

Its potential value lies not just in the Queen model itself, but in the network of data production, training, and applications built around it.

On the other hand, if the project only continues expanding its crawler network and training data without delivering better model performance or attracting real users, its long-term potential may struggle to translate into sustainable token value.

What I will be watching most closely is not how many webpages CRAWL can scrape, but whether it can train a Queen model that Crypto users genuinely find worth using.

OpenAI's ecosystem lead Vibhor Chhabra laid out where ChatGPT is going at DevDay. His thesis is that a conversation is often only the beginning of a task, and the goal is making capabilities feel like a natural part of working with ChatGPT.

1. Plugin Extensions. Partners bring interactive experiences into ChatGPT. Adobe: image edits with hands-on controls. tldraw: a shared canvas with the agent. MagicPath: interactive prototypes you can edit yourself.

2. A plugin can package skills, an MCP server, or both. Builders get three ways in: reusable workflow knowledge, live information, or actions that finish a task. Plugin Creator plus automated submission checks are new.

3. Discovery, ranking, and recommendations are getting better, in the directory and inside conversations. The stated goal is suggestions with good judgment about when they add value and when they get in the way.

4. MCP Events. Ask ChatGPT to watch for supported events, a new message or a document comment, and respond when they arrive. 5. ChatGPT Sites can now host MCP servers, including plugin extensions.

His honest caveat is that plenty of work remains on reliability, discovery, and developer experience. Ecosystem plays live or die on that, not the launch demos.

PerplexityはAIエージェントがコードを実行する際の「サンドボックス」環境を自社保有・自社最適化する方向に舵を切る。これは単なるクラウド借り上げではなく、ハードウェアレベルでの垂直統合戦略。

NVIDIAが開発する次世代CPU「Vera」（Vera Rubinプラットフォームの一部、Grace Hopperの後継系統）を指すとみられる。Arav氏は「Veraはx86より遥かに優れている」と明言しており、AIエージェント向けワークロードにおいてArmベースのカスタムシリコンがIntel/AMD系のx86アーキテクチャを上回るという強い主張。

Zhou Yuxiang hired food delivery riders to sell AI to factories. Now he’s chasing China’s industrial AI breakthrough | Nicholas Gordon, Fortune

When Zhou Yuxiang founded Black Lake Technologies, he did what seemed sensible: He trusted experience, hiring salespeople from traditional Western software companies like SAP and Siemens. But as the Shanghai-based AI startup moved from enterprise clients to China’s smaller factories—some 4 million of them—those polished professionals proved useless.

“They couldn’t even figure out how to get into the factory, past the security guard and the guard dogs,” Zhou recalled in an interview with Fortune during the Fortune Leaders Forum in Macau on Sept. 8.

So Zhou recruited his sales team from a different labor pool: food delivery riders. Couriers from Meituan and Alibaba’s https://t.co/xgd5QZisod “have the best, you know, street-smart wisdom to meet the decision-makers,” he explained. Drivers know the back entrances, the factory layouts, and the best path to the boss of a mom-and-pop workshop.

Still, what these drivers had in chutzpah, they lacked in actual product knowledge. So Zhou put every new hire through what he called a “devil boot camp”: five days of 14-hour training sessions, a daily exam, and one contract closed over the phone by the final day. Only about half graduated.

Zhou, a Dartmouth grad and former investment banker, is now betting that the most interesting market for AI isn’t the consumer smartphone nor the corporate office, but rather the shop floor. Black Lake’s product is factory-management software: a cloud-based system that tracks orders, schedules, materials, and output—and, more recently, AI agents that can read an incoming order, generate a quote, and schedule production on their own. Black Lake says it has been profitable since 2025 and that revenue has grown more than 60% a year.

China is the testing ground for that idea. It is also, so far, an unproven one. Zhou’s larger wager isn’t just that AI can make existing work faster, but also that it can restructure how an industry operates.

He doesn’t believe it’s happened yet, anywhere. “I don’t think the Google moment has happened yet in the AI era, because we are only replacing [tasks],” he said. “I don’t think we have restructured the industry.”

The factory data desert

Black Lake is actually Zhou’s second attempt at building a startup. In 2015, he and two high school friends returned to China to found MadaData, an analytics startup Zhou describes as “a Palantir for China.’ The idea was that, much like how Palantir sits on top of enterprise and government data, MadaData would sit on top of factory data.

It was a flop. “It turned out most of the factories that we visited back then had zero data,” Zhou says.

As the team liquidated MadaData, they were saved by a group of second-generation factory owners, “forced by their family to take over [the] family business.” Educated abroad like Zhou, they faced a market that was shifting toward smaller orders with faster turnarounds than the big, standardized runs their parents’ factories were built for.

This time, Zhou wanted hands-on experience. “We thought we should really go into the factory instead of locking ourselves up in the room and coding,” he said.

He took a job on a plastic-injection line at a factory that made cosmetics for a European giant, working alongside migrant laborers from less-developed provinces like Sichuan and Guizhou. Zhou timed what happened between batches, and found that, during a six-hour changeover, only one hour was useful. The rest was wasted owing to “subjective decision-making” and information silos.

China’s industrial AI advantage

China has perhaps become the world’s second most important source of AI innovation. After the U.S., open-weight models from Alibaba, DeepSeek, https://t.co/GBdSBxHbvh, and Moonshot AI now deliver near–frontier performance at a fraction of the cost of closed Western rivals. Much of that energy is being applied to manufacturing. China installed 354,000 industrial robots in 2025, a record 59% of the world’s total, according to the International Federation of Robotics.

Despite the hype, China’s AI sector faces some significant constraints on its growth. U.S. export controls still deny China access to the frontier AI processors. China’s funding pool is also far shallower: OpenAI raised $122 billion in a single round this year and Anthropic $65 billion, totals which no Chinese company can match.

But Zhou sees the biggest challenge as internal. “I think we’re racing against ourselves,” he said. “I probably look short of sleep today because we are really short of sleep … Time is the limited resource for us.”

Yet China is still playing catch-up with the West. “For Western countries, that digitization … took place for 40 to 50 years, since … the founding of software companies in the 1980s or 1990s,” Zhou said. “But in China, I think really the concept of digitization became a really recognized concept to factory owners only 10 years ago.”

The problem Zhou discovered when MadaData collapsed has not gone away. Onstage at the Fortune Leaders Forum, he dismissed the idea that China could leapfrog the process entirely. “People always have this wishful thinking that we’re going to skip the software time and go directly into AI, just like we skipped the credit card era into mobile payments,” he said. “Unfortunately, I think in China we still have a lot to do with digitization.”

As frontier models catch up with one another within weeks, data is becoming the differentiating factor in AI. “How do we prepare data? How do we accumulate data?” he asked onstage. “That has become an industry question.”

Chasing AI’s Google moment

For all the agents Black Lake has deployed, Zhou doesn’t believe AI has yet reached its “Google moment,” and changed how industries fundamentally work; so far it has replaced tasks, not business models.

His attempt at an answer is a new platform called PopZao, a website and WeChat mini program that Black Lake has incubated for two years. The proposition is to connect China’s factories with its creator economy; Black Lake’s agents bridge the gap by converting ideas into designs, a 3D simulation, and industrial data sent to a factory.

Zhou tied the idea to the craze around Labubu, the Pop Mart–owned toy that went viral in 2025, helping to spur a 185% jump in revenue for the toy store chain last year. PopZao, in theory, allows anyone with a following—now just massive IP machines—to develop merchandise.

One early customer of PopZao was a Buddhist temple which wanted new merchandise for its younger visitors. After the temple’s master submitted a photo of its stone lions, Black Lake designed and manufactured a small batch of 500 units in just 30 days; they sold out within a week. “Now the temple is taking pictures of trees, the dogs, cats, different kinds of things as their souvenirs,” Zhou said.

Zhou won’t yet claim that constitutes AI’s breakthrough moment.“The real Google moment should happen only when you restructure the industry rather than replace human beings,” he said onstage at the Fortune Leaders Forum. “This is what I’m working so hard to see—whether the Google moment can happen sooner than later in our industry.”

Nvidia’s new $150 billion buyback authorization is obviously a huge number.

But the size of the authorization is not really what caught my attention.

What matters more to me is that Nvidia can even consider returning this much capital while still spending aggressively to support its AI growth.

The company now has about $235 billion remaining under its repurchase programme, which it expects to use through fiscal 2028.

That does not mean $235 billion will suddenly disappear from the balance sheet. An authorization is only permission to buy shares, not a commitment to spend the full amount immediately.

The more interesting part is the cash generation behind it.

In the first half of fiscal 2027, Nvidia generated $74.4 billion in operating cash flow and spent $39.8 billion buying back its own shares.

That is almost as much as the $40.4 billion it repurchased during the entire previous fiscal year.

For me, that says more about the business than the headline buyback number itself.

Nvidia is generating enough cash to invest heavily in AI infrastructure, keep expanding the business and still return tens of billions of dollars to shareholders.

But I would not automatically call that good capital allocation.

Buybacks create more value when shares are purchased at attractive prices. When the valuation is already high, the question becomes harder.

So I would not judge this programme by how large it is.

I would judge it by whether Nvidia’s earnings and free cash flow keep growing fast enough to make those repurchases sensible at the prices being paid.

The buyback tells me Nvidia has enormous financial capacity.

What I want to know is whether the underlying business keeps growing fast enough to make that capital allocation worthwhile.

雙向頻寬的極限破局：語音咒語、二維拓樸，與中文在人機協同中的底層優勢

當前生成式 AI 的技術演進，正在悄然完成一場人機介面的「權力位移」。

特斯拉前 AI 總監 Andrej Karpathy 近期提出一個關鍵觀察：隨著模型推論與代理人架構（Agentic Workflows）日趨成熟，AI 承擔了絕大多數的繁重執行工作（legwork），人機協同的真正瓶頸已徹底逆轉為「人類理解與審計輸出的時間與認知成本」。為了解決這個瓶頸，他提倡利用受控語言（如 ASD-STE100）、二維圖表、互動式網頁乃至動態解說影片等「即拋型軟體工件（discardable software artifacts）」，來加速人類對模型高維輸出的吸收。
然而，Karpathy 的論述僅揭示了問題的後半段——輸出端的降維與解碼。如果將人機協同視為一個完整的控制論閉環（Cybernetic Loop），那麼決定這個系統運作上限的，實則是「輸入端的語義錨定」與「輸出端的認知吸收」兩大物理頻寬如何對稱匹配。

這場頻寬革命的深層邏輯，不僅重構了未來的 Prompt 範式，更揭示了一個長期被忽視的本質問題：為什麼在高度依賴語音輸入與空間拓樸的新一代 AI 範式中，中文相較於拼音文字，具備顯著的底層結構優勢？

一、 輸入端的典範轉移：語音長文本的「完整先於精準」

長久以來，大眾對 AI 輸入的理解停留在「提示詞工程（Prompt Engineering）的精煉化」，試圖用極簡的關鍵字或固定的模板去撬動模型。這種習慣本質上是物理鍵盤輸入時代的妥協產物——因為手指敲擊的輸入速率極低（每分鐘約 40 至 80 字），迫使人類必須在輸入前先在腦中進行高損耗的資訊壓縮。

然而，這完全違背了大型語言模型的運作第一性原理。

LLM 實質上是在數千維的潛在空間（Latent Space）中進行機率分佈推論。一個過度簡化、缺乏邊界條件的簡短 Prompt，本質上是在語義空間中留下巨大的資訊真空，迫使模型只能依賴統計先驗進行隨機填補，這正是幻覺與空泛回覆的主要根源。

要精確鎖定模型的高維推論軌道，最有效的方式並非字句的精修，而是語義重力場的建立。這要求輸入必須具備極高的「上下文質量與張力」——包含完整的事實背景、程序階段、邊界限制、價值偏好與潛在抗辯。

這正是為什麼「語音輸入」是未來與 AI 互動不可逆的核心能力：

 * 輸入頻寬的倍數級躍升：口語表達的輸出速率可達每分鐘 200 至 300 字，是鍵盤輸入的數倍。
 * 思維完整性先於精準度：在語音輸入的範式下，核心準則是「完整先於精準（Completeness precedes Precision）」。先透過連續不中斷的語音串流，將腦中龐大的思維網絡完整傾倒進上下文視窗（Context Window），構建出無損的語義邊界。精準度是修正性的，而完整度是基礎性的；缺乏完整度的精準，只是局部的偽精緻。

最近 GitHub 上有个项目 OpenRig，它把 Codex、Claude Code 这些 Coding Agent 组织成一个长期工作的AI团队。

以前我们用 Codex，通常是：提任务 → Codex执行 → 检查。OpenRig 可以变成：
我提任务
↓
Owner Agent负责接任务
↓
执行Agent完成工作
↓
Checker Agent独立检查
↓
发现问题继续修改
↓
最后把结果交给我

官方目前已经提供现成的双Agent组合。可以用两个 Codex，也可以让 Claude Code负责执行 + Codex负责检查。

比如我要做一个网页，可以直接给 Owner：“帮我做一个AI工具导航页。要求：
先制定任务计划；
完成网页；
交给Checker检查；
检查功能、页面和错误；
有问题先修改；
全部完成后再告诉我结果。”

这样我不需要同时盯着几个Agent。只需要跟一个负责人说需求，Agent之间自己分工。

新手第一次可以这样跑：
安装 OpenRig
→ 建一个测试项目
→ 启动双Agent
→ 给Owner一个小任务
→ Owner执行
→ Checker检查
→ 看最终结果

它现在还属于比较早期的项目，而且安装有一定门槛。目前官方主要支持 macOS/Linux，需要 Node.js 和 tmux，Windows 原生暂不支持。

这个方向很值得关注：以前我们学的是“怎么用一个Agent”，接下来可能要学“怎么管理一群Agent”。

@axisrobotics到底有多火，看数据就知道：

8 月底，Axis 积累 470 万条有效机器人操作轨迹，注册用户超过 20 万。

9 月份数据继续上涨，10 月 2 号，官方数据已经突破 600 万条，而且还在持续增长。

以前给机器人提供训练数据，基本上要靠实验室、机械臂，还要专业人员反复操作才可以。

Axis 则直接把这套流程搬进浏览器里，只要照着任务抓取、摆放、堆叠，就能贡献机器人训练需要的动作数据。

而且他们的 Franka 机器人仿真数据集在 Hugging Face 上累计下载超过 16 万次。

在官方公布的测试中，使用这批数据继续训练后，π0.5 模型在 LIBERO-Plus 基准上的成功率从 83.9% 提升到 88.8%。并且随着训练数据的增加，表现还在提升。

至于9 月的社区销售打新，原计划募集 100 万美元，最终有 2472 人参与，总投入超 239.4 万美元，超额认购 2.39 倍。

论文也入选了 IROS 2026 的相关研讨会，并在10 月 1 日进行了展示。

600 万条轨迹只是一个阶段。是这些数据能不能持续提升模型表现，以及训练出来的能力能不能真正落到现实机器人身上。

arXiv 上 2026-10-01 的預印本（2610.01365，未經同行評審）提出 ReGap：不給答案，不給種子資料，只讓模型自己生成候選、按答案詞機率篩一遍，再低秩適配一次。

六個設定（GPT-2、OPT、Qwen3）上，一輪就讓目標關聯恢復率比原本高出 6 到 21 個百分點。

最要緊的是那組對照：同一個適配器，套在「以前見過目標」的檢查點上，恢復率從 42% 升到 63%；套在從沒見過目標的檢查點上，零增益。

也就是說，它叫醒的東西本來就在裡面，只是原本問不出來。

作者也寫了邊界：隨機綁定的關聯、或做過 NPO 遺忘之後，恢復大幅減弱。所以這不是「刪了等於沒刪」。

難處理的地方在這裡：「已刪除」在合規文件上成立，在工程上不一定。兩件事同時為真，而且沒人說謊。
